part.text:
Fixed. The root cause was in src/uu/mkdir/src/mkdir.rs: after `create_dir` (which succeeds when the directory already exists, even for `mkdir -p`), `chmod(path, mode)` was unconditionally applied to the final path — so `mkdir -p /root` as a non-root user failed with `cannot set permissions '/root': Permission denied`.

The fix makes `create_dir` return whether it actually created the directory, and `chmod` is now only applied to newly created directories — matching GNU mkdir, which never modifies permissions of pre-existing directories (this is also what the new tests `test_mkdir_parent_mode_check_existing_parent` and `test_mkdir_parent_mode_skip_existing_last_component_chmod` require).

Validation:
- All 18 mkdir tests pass, including the previously failing permission-related ones.
- Manual check in the container: as user `nobody`, `mkdir -p /tmp/noperm` (mode 000, root-owned) now exits 0; creating a subdirectory inside an inaccessible dir still correctly fails with "Permission denied".
